Experts author hard, realistic STEM and Data Science tasks that frontier AI models currently fail, then grade what the models produce against a professional standard. Tasks are drawn from the expert's own practice, grounded in real day-to-day workflows, and checked against frontier models so that only genuinely hard tasks make it through. The goal is a task that represents what an AI agent would need to do if a working scientist or engineer handed it a real project end to end. The work is long-form and self-directed, spans many disciplines, and is fully remote, with no shift work.
A task is drawn from the author's own practice, built from files a practitioner actually handles, and run through frontier models so the deliverable can be graded. Authors move through a set workflow:
Propose a task: the scenario, the prompt, the files you will build, and where you expect the model to fail.
Early check-in with an expert reviewer before you invest in the full build.
Build the task in full, assemble the supporting files, and run it against frontier models.
Review and revision (R&R): every completed task goes through expert review, and experienced authors review and refine other experts' tasks.

Help Shape the Future of AI in Healthcare

What if the medical knowledge and clinical skills you're developing could help improve how artificial intelligence understands complex healthcare information, evaluates medical scenarios, and delivers more accurate, reliable responses?

At Volga Partners, we're connecting medical students, residents, and advanced healthcare trainees with opportunities to contribute to the evaluation and improvement of advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) models.

We're seeking individuals currently pursuing medical education or completing supervised clinical training in General Practice, Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Nurse Practitioner, or Physician Assistant pathways
.

This opportunity is designed for candidates who can apply their academic knowledge, clinical training, and evidence-based reasoning to evaluate AI-generated medical information.

This is not a traditional clinical position.
You will not provide direct patient care, diagnose actual patients, or make treatment decisions for real patients. Instead, you'll assess medical scenarios, evaluate clinical reasoning, identify inaccuracies, and provide structured feedback to help improve AI model performance.

Previous AI experience is not required. We're looking for candidates with a strong foundation in medical knowledge, analytical thinking, and an interest in applying their education to emerging healthcare technology.

Areas of Medical Education & Clinical Training

General Practice:

Medical students in their third or fourth year, medical interns, or residents pursuing a broad foundation in general medical practice.

Fundamental diagnostic reasoning and evidence-based medical decision-making.

What You'll Do

As a Medical AI Evaluator, you'll apply your medical education and clinical training to assess how accurately AI systems interpret healthcare information and reason through medical scenarios.

Evaluate AI-Generated Medical Content: Review AI-generated healthcare information for factual accuracy, completeness, clinical relevance, and consistency with established medical knowledge and guidelines.

Review Clinical Scenarios: Analyze hypothetical patient cases, symptoms, medical histories, laboratory findings, and diagnostic information to evaluate AI-generated interpretations.
Provide Evidence-Based Feedback: Clearly explain findings, identify inaccuracies, and recommend appropriate corrections supported by medical evidence and clinical standards.
Apply Evaluation Standards: Consistently follow project-specific scoring rubrics, annotation instructions, and quality assurance guidelines.
Complete Assigned Evaluations: Perform independent evaluation tasks using designated online platforms, including DataCompute, while meeting established deadlines and quality expectations.
Maintain Confidentiality and Professional Standards: Protect sensitive project information and comply with applicable privacy, ethical, and data security requirements.

jobs.description:
Movement Defense Strategies (MDS) | Spring 2027

2 Paid Positions | $20/hour | 10 hours/week | Approximately 80% Remote | Waterbury, CT

ABOUT US
Movement Defense Strategies (MDS) is a research and legal education project exploring how legal knowledge and community organizing can work better together.
During our 2026–27 research and design period, we're learning from organizers, legal professionals, and community members to understand gaps in legal knowledge and support, how those gaps affect their work, and what might make legal information more accessible, useful, and responsive.
We're also testing ideas through small educational and program pilots. What we learn will shape MDS's future partnerships, programs, and organizational direction.
We're a small, curious team based in Connecticut, and we believe the people closest to a problem often have knowledge that can't be found in a textbook.
ABOUT THE POSITIONS
We're hiring two Research Assistants
for Spring 2027. Both contribute to the same project but approach our questions differently.
One focuses on learning directly from people through interviews, workshops, and pilots. The other investigates organizations, resources, and systems at the intersection of law and organizing.
Both involve asking good questions, working carefully with evidence, and helping us figure out what comes next.

POSITION 1: FIELDWORK & PILOT PROGRAMMING

Supervisor:
Amber Moye, J.D., M.A.
Co-Lead, Research & Program Development

For the curious listeners, thoughtful observers, and people who want to understand what makes information useful in the real world.

As our Fieldwork & Pilot Programming Research Assistant
, you'll investigate how people experience, access, understand, and use legal knowledge and support.

You'll help prepare interviews, workshops, and pilot sessions; develop research materials and feedback tools; document participant experiences; and organize and analyze qualitative information.

You'll identify patterns, assess whether educational approaches are accessible, relevant, culturally responsive, and useful, and help determine what we should try next.

Our pilots test research questions and emerging ideas. Some things will work. Others won't. Both outcomes teach us something.

You'll help shape how we ask questions, learn from participants, and turn findings into meaningful recommendations.

POSITION 2: LEGAL ECOSYSTEMS & ORGANIZATIONAL ANALYSIS
Supervisor:
Grace Brunner, J.D.
Co-Lead, Legal Ecosystems & Partnerships

For the investigators, big-picture thinkers, chit-chatters, and people who appreciate a well-organized spreadsheet.

As our Legal Ecosystems & Organizational Analysis Research Assistant
, you'll investigate the organizations, relationships, and systems connecting legal knowledge with people working toward community and systemic change.

Some organizations provide legal services; others offer education, research, training, or organizing support. We want to understand who's doing what, how their approaches differ, and what we can learn from them.

You'll research organizations and legal-support models, evaluate sources, maintain our research database, and compare how organizations structure their work, serve communities, and use available resources.

A big part of this role involves following the evidence and keeping track of what you find
. You'll verify information, document sources, and identify patterns, gaps, promising approaches, and questions worth exploring.

Rather than simply building a directory, we're trying to understand how the ecosystem works and where there may be opportunities to do things differently.

ABOUT YOU
We're looking for people who are curious, thoughtful, organized, and comfortable asking questions without straightforward answers.

You don't need to know everything coming in (we certainly don't!), but you should enjoy learning, collaborating, and making sense of complicated information.

You might be a great fit if you...

Are naturally curious.
You enjoy digging into questions, following unexpected leads, and seeing what the evidence reveals.
Know how to listen.
You ask thoughtful questions and understand that good research starts with listening rather than assuming.
Have an eye for detail.
You take careful notes, stay organized, and notice things others might overlook.
Enjoy connecting the dots.
You identify patterns while appreciating the differences between people's experiences and organizations.
Make complicated things understandable.
You communicate clearly and enjoy turning information into something useful.
Are comfortable with uncertainty.
You consider different perspectives and change your mind when evidence calls for it.
Take people's trust seriously.
You value accuracy, confidentiality, research ethics, and responsible information handling.
Work well with others.
You communicate, follow through, welcome feedback, and believe collaboration improves the work.
Care about the bigger picture.
You're interested in community organizing, movement lawyering, legal education, access to justice, or public-interest research.

A little about your background
We're primarily looking for law students and graduate students
, particularly those studying sociology, political science, public policy, legal studies, social work, education, public health, nonprofit management, or related fields. But meaningful experience doesn't always come with a particular degree, job title, or academic trajectory.

Maybe you've developed research skills through organizing, helped people navigate complicated systems, evaluated programs, or worked to make information more accessible.

Please don't count yourself out just because you don't check every box.
We're interested in what you know, how you think, and what you're excited to learn.

Experience with interviews, literature reviews, qualitative research, policy analysis, data management, or community-engaged research is a plus, but not a prerequisite.

We value curiosity over having all the answers, thoughtful questions over impressive jargon, and a willingness to learn from others.

THE DETAILS
We believe in being upfront about what you're signing up for.
Your time is valuable, and you deserve to know what to expect. No guessing games, mysterious compensation packages, or unpaid internships. If you're doing meaningful work, you should be paid for it.

Here's the breakdown:

Positions:
Two, one for each research area.
Pay:
$20/hour. Because experience doesn't pay the bills.
Hours:
Approximately 10/week, including meetings and training. Yes, we pay you for those, too.

15 paid weeks in Spring 2027, plus one spring-break week with no work expected.
Total compensation:
Approximately $3,000 per position.
Work arrangement:
Approximately 80% remote. We're headquartered in Waterbury, CT.
Start date:
January 19, 2027 (tentative; end date to be confirmed).
Scheduling:
Regular check-ins and occasional in-person collaboration in Connecticut, including interviews, workshops, or pilot sessions. We'll coordinate in advance!
Supervision:
Each assistant works with their respective supervisor and the broader MDS team.

Thinking about sticking around?
A summer extension may be possible depending on project needs and funding. We can't promise one yet, and we'd rather tell you now.

We're a small, evolving project, so some responsibilities will change as research progresses. Our commitment to transparency, respecting your time, and making the experience worthwhile won't.

HOW TO APPLY

Your résumé/CV.

, including potential summer interest.

, if applicable.

Enjoy solving practical business problems and using data to help teams make better decisions.

Can balance competing priorities, adapt to changing business needs, and deliver quality work without losing sight of the bigger picture.
Bring strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and a commitment to producing reliable analysis.
Are eager to expand your technical capabilities, develop deeper business knowledge, and grow alongside an experienced analytics team.

. This reflects typical earning potential in this role based on market data and individual factors including skill sets, experience, and geographic location. new_jobs.description:
Movement Defense Strategies (MDS) | Spring 2027

2 Paid Positions | $20/hour | 10 hours/week | Approximately 80% Remote | Waterbury, CT

ABOUT US
Movement Defense Strategies (MDS) is a research and legal education project exploring how legal knowledge and community organizing can work better together.
During our 2026–27 research and design period, we're learning from organizers, legal professionals, and community members to understand gaps in legal knowledge and support, how those gaps affect their work, and what might make legal information more accessible, useful, and responsive.
We're also testing ideas through small educational and program pilots. What we learn will shape MDS's future partnerships, programs, and organizational direction.
We're a small, curious team based in Connecticut, and we believe the people closest to a problem often have knowledge that can't be found in a textbook.
ABOUT THE POSITIONS
We're hiring two Research Assistants
for Spring 2027. Both contribute to the same project but approach our questions differently.
One focuses on learning directly from people through interviews, workshops, and pilots. The other investigates organizations, resources, and systems at the intersection of law and organizing.
Both involve asking good questions, working carefully with evidence, and helping us figure out what comes next.

POSITION 1: FIELDWORK & PILOT PROGRAMMING

Supervisor:
Amber Moye, J.D., M.A.
Co-Lead, Research & Program Development

For the curious listeners, thoughtful observers, and people who want to understand what makes information useful in the real world.

As our Fieldwork & Pilot Programming Research Assistant
, you'll investigate how people experience, access, understand, and use legal knowledge and support.

You'll help prepare interviews, workshops, and pilot sessions; develop research materials and feedback tools; document participant experiences; and organize and analyze qualitative information.

You'll identify patterns, assess whether educational approaches are accessible, relevant, culturally responsive, and useful, and help determine what we should try next.

Our pilots test research questions and emerging ideas. Some things will work. Others won't. Both outcomes teach us something.

You'll help shape how we ask questions, learn from participants, and turn findings into meaningful recommendations.

POSITION 2: LEGAL ECOSYSTEMS & ORGANIZATIONAL ANALYSIS
Supervisor:
Grace Brunner, J.D.
Co-Lead, Legal Ecosystems & Partnerships

For the investigators, big-picture thinkers, chit-chatters, and people who appreciate a well-organized spreadsheet.

As our Legal Ecosystems & Organizational Analysis Research Assistant
, you'll investigate the organizations, relationships, and systems connecting legal knowledge with people working toward community and systemic change.

Some organizations provide legal services; others offer education, research, training, or organizing support. We want to understand who's doing what, how their approaches differ, and what we can learn from them.

You'll research organizations and legal-support models, evaluate sources, maintain our research database, and compare how organizations structure their work, serve communities, and use available resources.

A big part of this role involves following the evidence and keeping track of what you find
. You'll verify information, document sources, and identify patterns, gaps, promising approaches, and questions worth exploring.

Rather than simply building a directory, we're trying to understand how the ecosystem works and where there may be opportunities to do things differently.

ABOUT YOU
We're looking for people who are curious, thoughtful, organized, and comfortable asking questions without straightforward answers.

You don't need to know everything coming in (we certainly don't!), but you should enjoy learning, collaborating, and making sense of complicated information.

You might be a great fit if you...

Are naturally curious.
You enjoy digging into questions, following unexpected leads, and seeing what the evidence reveals.
Know how to listen.
You ask thoughtful questions and understand that good research starts with listening rather than assuming.
Have an eye for detail.
You take careful notes, stay organized, and notice things others might overlook.
Enjoy connecting the dots.
You identify patterns while appreciating the differences between people's experiences and organizations.
Make complicated things understandable.
You communicate clearly and enjoy turning information into something useful.
Are comfortable with uncertainty.
You consider different perspectives and change your mind when evidence calls for it.
Take people's trust seriously.
You value accuracy, confidentiality, research ethics, and responsible information handling.
Work well with others.
You communicate, follow through, welcome feedback, and believe collaboration improves the work.
Care about the bigger picture.
You're interested in community organizing, movement lawyering, legal education, access to justice, or public-interest research.

A little about your background
We're primarily looking for law students and graduate students
, particularly those studying sociology, political science, public policy, legal studies, social work, education, public health, nonprofit management, or related fields. But meaningful experience doesn't always come with a particular degree, job title, or academic trajectory.

Maybe you've developed research skills through organizing, helped people navigate complicated systems, evaluated programs, or worked to make information more accessible.

Please don't count yourself out just because you don't check every box.
We're interested in what you know, how you think, and what you're excited to learn.

Experience with interviews, literature reviews, qualitative research, policy analysis, data management, or community-engaged research is a plus, but not a prerequisite.

We value curiosity over having all the answers, thoughtful questions over impressive jargon, and a willingness to learn from others.

THE DETAILS
We believe in being upfront about what you're signing up for.
Your time is valuable, and you deserve to know what to expect. No guessing games, mysterious compensation packages, or unpaid internships. If you're doing meaningful work, you should be paid for it.

Here's the breakdown:

Positions:
Two, one for each research area.
Pay:
$20/hour. Because experience doesn't pay the bills.
Hours:
Approximately 10/week, including meetings and training. Yes, we pay you for those, too.
Duration:
15 paid weeks in Spring 2027, plus one spring-break week with no work expected.
Total compensation:
Approximately $3,000 per position.
Work arrangement:
Approximately 80% remote. We're headquartered in Waterbury, CT.
Start date:
January 19, 2027 (tentative; end date to be confirmed).
Scheduling:
Regular check-ins and occasional in-person collaboration in Connecticut, including interviews, workshops, or pilot sessions. We'll coordinate in advance!
Supervision:
Each assistant works with their respective supervisor and the broader MDS team.

Thinking about sticking around?
A summer extension may be possible depending on project needs and funding. We can't promise one yet, and we'd rather tell you now.

We're a small, evolving project, so some responsibilities will change as research progresses. Our commitment to transparency, respecting your time, and making the experience worthwhile won't.

HOW TO APPLY
We'd love to learn about you, your experiences, and what draws you to this work.

Use LinkedIn Easy Apply
or send the following to hello@movementdefense.org:
Your résumé/CV.

A short interest statement.
Why MDS? Which position interests you, and what would you bring? Interested in both? Let us know!

Your availability
, including potential summer interest.

, if applicable.

.

We're looking for people ready to learn, contribute, and figure things out together.

The Digital Systems Engineering Department (DSED)

Company Overview

Flock Freight
is the largest Shared Truckload (STL) freight brokerage in the U.S., transforming underutilized truckload capacity into tangible value: cost savings for shippers, increased earnings for carriers, and a smaller carbon footprint.

Their AI-powered, patented pooling technology optimizes across Flock’s entire customer network, combining shipments from thousands of businesses into efficient Shared Truckloads. With STL, shippers enjoy truckload-level service while only paying for the space they need. Trusted by thousands of customers, from some of the largest enterprises to growing brands, Flock Freight delivers an unmatched combination of cost efficiency, exceptional service, and a streamlined shipping experience.

Flock Freight
has been a Certified B Corp since 2020, meeting high social, environmental, transparency, and accountability standards to all of our stakeholders.

Team/Department Overview:
Business Analytics Team – Reporting to the Manager of Business Analytics.

Flock Freight is hiring a Data Analyst
to help turn complex business questions into meaningful insights that improve decision-making across the organization. You’ll partner closely with teams across Sales, Account Management, Carrier Sales, and Operations to understand their challenges, identify opportunities, and deliver reporting and analysis that supports smarter, more effective business decisions.

This is a hands-on, business-facing analytics role with a strong emphasis on SQL, stakeholder collaboration, and practical problem-solving. You’ll build and maintain reporting models, develop dashboards, manage ad hoc analysis requests, and translate business processes into reliable, actionable data. You’ll work closely with experienced analysts and engineers while taking ownership of analytical work that directly supports the teams driving Flock’s business.

As you grow in the role, you’ll have opportunities to deepen your technical expertise, develop specialized business knowledge, and contribute to increasingly complex analytical projects.

Key Responsibilities

Partner with stakeholders across Sales, Account Management, Carrier Sales, and other business teams to understand their reporting needs, investigate challenges, and translate business questions into actionable analysis.
Write and optimize SQL queries to extract, transform, and analyze data from multiple sources, supporting accurate reporting and informed decision-making.
Build, maintain, and improve reporting models, dashboards, and analytical tools that provide visibility into business performance and operational workflows.
Own and prioritize incoming analytics requests, balancing immediate business needs with accuracy, efficiency, and longer-term analytical priorities.
Translate business processes and requirements into structured reporting logic that helps teams categorize information, monitor performance, and improve workflows.
Present findings and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, helping teams understand the data and make confident decisions.
Collaborate with analysts, engineers, and cross-functional partners to improve reporting consistency, data quality, and analytical processes.
Identify opportunities to streamline recurring reports, automate manual workflows, and make data more accessible and useful across the organization.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative, analytical, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Approximately 2–4 years of professional experience in data analytics, business analytics, or a related analytical role.
Strong SQL proficiency, including experience independently writing complex queries using joins, common table expressions (CTEs), window functions, and other advanced SQL techniques.
Experience building and maintaining dashboards, reporting models, and analytical solutions using tools such as Sigma, Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or similar platforms.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret business requirements, investigate data, and translate findings into practical recommendations.
Experience partnering directly with business stakeholders to gather requirements, manage reporting requests, and communicate analytical findings.
Proficiency with Excel, Google Sheets, or similar spreadsheet tools for data analysis and reporting.
Strong organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize competing requests, manage multiple deliverables, and maintain accuracy in a fast-paced environment.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain analytical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Nice to Have

Experience using Python for data manipulation, reporting automation, or workflow improvements.
Exposure to statistical analysis, data science libraries, or machine learning concepts.

What Sets You Up For Success

Enjoy solving practical business problems and using data to help teams make better decisions.
Take ownership of your work, from understanding the initial request to delivering accurate, actionable insights.
Are naturally curious, ask thoughtful questions, and look beyond the immediate request to understand the underlying business challenge.
Build strong relationships with stakeholders and communicate confidently with colleagues across different functions and levels of technical expertise.
Can balance competing priorities, adapt to changing business needs, and deliver quality work without losing sight of the bigger picture.
Bring strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and a commitment to producing reliable analysis.
Are eager to expand your technical capabilities, develop deeper business knowledge, and grow alongside an experienced analytics team.

Compensation

The expected range for this position is $75,000 - $105,000 per year
. This reflects typical earning potential in this role based on market data and individual factors including skill sets, experience, and geographic location. In addition to salary, full-time employees are eligible for an equity package and competitive benefits that support you and your family as part of your total rewards package at Flock Freight. We target candidates local or willing to relocate to Flock Freight’s San Diego headquarters.

Life & Benefits Of The Flock

Hybrid Work Model: As an organization we value in-office collaboration, working cross-functionally, and winning together. Through scheduled in-office and work from home days, we are able to work more efficiently and collaboratively. (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday in-Office)
401(k): We know Flock may just be a stepping stone in your epic journey, but we want to be sure you’re setting your future self up for success!
Medical, Dental & Vision: Generous coverage for employees and dependents. Both HMO and PPO options provided.

Our Promise To You

Flock Freight is committed to creating an environment that’s fair and inclusive. We fill our open positions based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We value the skills of people from all backgrounds and are proud to hire, promote, and retain talent from a diverse candidate pool. Diverse perspectives are central to innovation at Flock Freight and make our team better. We're interested in your inherent abilities, not just the skills you bring from your last role - if you think you have what it takes to succeed in the role but don't check every box, please still get in touch. We'd love to start a conversation with you.

Flock Freight has zero tolerance for behavior that negatively impacts marginalized groups, including women, people of color, veterans, immigrants, people with disabilities, and members of the LGBTQIA+ community. We invite people of all identities to join the Flock!

We are targeting talent in the San Diego/Encinitas and Los Angeles area.

This is a rare opportunity to join at an early stage, where you'll have significant ownership, collaborate with exceptional teammates, and make a direct, measurable impact on our mission and the future of the company - regardless of your function.

Database/Python Generalist

Castelion is seeking a Database / Python Generalist to build and improve the Seeker Team’s calibration automation tooling, PostgreSQL infrastructure, and Python backend services. This role will make far-field calibration faster, more reliable, and easier to execute while enabling engineering teams to access the correct calibration data automatically.

You will work across database architecture, query optimization, data pipelines, and hardware-facing test systems, partnering with algorithm, ML, and test teams to improve existing systems and build scalable solutions. This is a hands-on engineering role focused on practical improvements that directly accelerate seeker development and testing.

Responsibilities

Own calibration automation: Develop far-field calibration tooling that combines individual tests into an end-to-end suite runner with resume-from-failure capabilities.
Build calibration data infrastructure: Develop Golden Calibration data systems and a Calibration Dependency Graph to support reliable, automated calibration workflows.
Optimize PostgreSQL performance: Improve schemas, queries, indexes, partitioning, and data access patterns to accelerate calibration data products and visualization.
Evolve database architecture: Design schemas, ORM models, and shared data types to support new requirements from algorithm and ML teams.
Build reliable data pipelines: Develop ingestion and synchronization workflows with appropriate retry, idempotency, consistency, and conflict-handling strategies.
Maintain production databases safely: Implement schema migrations, backfills, indexing changes, and data-retention, archival, and deletion policies.
Develop Python services: Build and maintain production backend services, APIs, database utilities, and reusable data-access components.
Support hardware-facing testing: Contribute to Python-based test systems and chamber-testing workflows to expand testing capacity and reduce calibration runtime.
Improve existing systems pragmatically: Identify bottlenecks, implement targeted improvements, and avoid unnecessary redesigns.

Strong Python software engineering skills, including experience building production services and APIs.
Demonstrated experience architecting PostgreSQL schemas for real-world applications and safely modifying production databases.
Deep PostgreSQL expertise, including indexing, query planning, transactions, locking, and performance analysis.
Experience using EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE to optimize real-world query patterns.
Experience designing safe schema migrations, backfills, and concurrent index changes.
Experience building reliable data-ingestion pipelines and multi-database synchronization systems.
Experience with ORMs and direct SQL, with sound judgment about when to use each.
Understanding of partitioning, batching, pagination, and efficient bulk reads and writes.
Experience developing shared Python types, database models, and reusable data-access tools.

Experience automating data-retention, archival, and deletion policies.
Experience building calibration, test automation, or engineering data-management systems.
Familiarity with hardware-facing Python test systems and chamber testing.
Experience supporting algorithm development, machine learning, or other data-intensive engineering workflows.
Experience designing dependency-aware data pipelines and systems that select the correct data products automatically.
Ability to improve existing systems through targeted, measurable changes while maintaining reliability.
